sections.heading: Why do the scores differ slightly on Salt and Iron?
paragraphs: The difference is small and runs in the audience direction. Converted to one scale, IMDb reads {{imdbX10}} and Rotten Tomatoes reads {{rt}}, so the audience side is slightly higher, with a small gap of {{gapAbs}} points. Critics and viewers mostly agree on the broad verdict.

Vote volume offers one explanation worth testing. With {{votes}} IMDb votes the audience number is steady, while the critic percentage counts each review as simply positive or not. A film with many mildly positive reviews and some lukewarm ones can sit a few points under its star rating.

Metascore points to the same mild difference. At {{metascore}} it sits below both main numbers, which hints that weighted critic scores are a touch cooler than the share of positive reviews. That is a small observation and should not be pushed further.

Genre gives context. The median difference for the {{genreCount}} {{genre}} films in this set is {{genreMedianGap}}, so {{title}} at {{gap}} sits slightly closer to agreement than the typical {{genre}} film here. [Our guide to the two scores](/compare/imdb-vs-rotten-tomatoes) explains why such small differences are normal.

sections.heading: Who should consider Salt and Iron?
paragraphs: If you pick films by consensus, this one is easy: the scores mostly agree, so either source leads you to the same expectation. If you favor action with some emotional weight, note that OMDb lists the second genre as drama, and the audience side being slightly higher may reflect that.
It is a full-length feature with an R rating, so check the rating before choosing it for a mixed group. The numbers point to a steady middle-of-the-road reception, and they say nothing about taste.

A useful habit with close scores is to look at the vote count before the percentages. Here {{votes}} votes stand behind the audience number, so it is a settled figure rather than an early reading, and that makes the mild difference a fairer description of how viewers feel.

sections.heading: How much should a small difference matter?
paragraphs: Not much. A few points on a shared scale can come from rounding, from the day the data were pulled, or from how each site counts. We flag the difference because it is measurable, not because it changes the picture. If you remember one thing, remember that this film sits close to agreement in the set, with neither group far from the other.
